primary_claim: LayerNorm can be removed from all GPT-2 models up to XL (1.5B parameters) via fine-tuning with only a small increase in cross-entropy loss (e.g. +0.0253 for XL), showing LN plays no substantial role in language modeling, though contrary to expectations attribution patching accuracy does not improve in LN-free models even as direct logit attribution becomes exact and entropy neurons stop functioning.

effect.metric: cross-entropy loss increase, LN-free vs vanilla fine-tuned model, on The Pile-filtered

contradicts_or_qualifies: Their own expectation that attribution patching would become more accurate in LN-free models; contrary to this, they find no improvement
Prior LN removal-by-fine-tuning work limited to GPT-2 Small, which they scale to GPT-2 XL (1.5B params) with improved training stability
stated_future_work: Support for other model families (e.g. Pythia) is a major followup, requiring monkey-patched forward passes, retuned hyperparameters, and distributed training for larger models
Gathering more data to establish confident empirical scaling laws for the removal schedule
limitations_stated: Training instability: the removal procedure is still unstable despite EMA recomputation and auxiliary-loss improvements; hyperparameter tuning and checkpoint recovery are often needed
Data and compute: still requires ~1% of original training data and compute for GPT-2 XL despite roughly 4x efficiency improvement
Small but consistent performance gap in LN-free models, and GPT-2 XL LN-free performs substantially worse on a tiny subset of Pile examples
Did not gather enough data to be confident in empirical scaling laws
quote: Contrary to our expectations, we saw no improvement resulting from removing LayerNorm.
